turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at twenty to five, so let's use the time. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first, so start by explaining that.
Thank you for coming. First, Owen should never have found out from his phone. I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you, and our procedure says I should have. I'm sorry.
Okay. Go on.
What time did Owen go to bed on Wednesday the 28th? Do you know?
Why are you asking me about Owen's bedtime? You're his English teacher. Answer my question first: what have you got on the essay itself?

The document's version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in a single edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 words in a single edit. Then 23 minutes of font, name and spacing changes. No earlier drafts anywhere in the history.
Hale, you just read me times and word counts. Those are the first real numbers I've heard today. Show me that version history on the screen, and tell me who has seen it besides you.
I'm waiting, Hale. The screen, and who else has seen it.

Here, on my laptop, the version history panel. Only me so far. Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the Folger text, tabbed, and you can search it on your phone.
Turn it toward me. I want to see the search myself.
What are you doing right now? Describe it for me, you've gone quiet and you're looking at your phone.
That's mine, Hale. Answer me: is the line in the Folger text, yes or no?

No. Search 'kingdom in exile' on the Folger site: zero results. Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues 'epistemological paralysis' and never mentions cowardice. Here's the outline, dated, his name on it.
Show me the outline. Dated, his name on it, and the page where it says cowardice.

Fourth. On November 2, after class, I asked Owen about the essay for five minutes. I wrote notes that day. I asked what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck.' I asked which scene his second paragraph was about. He couldn't say. How long have we been talking, by the way?
Fifteen minutes, roughly, and I've got a call at twenty to five. Your notes from November 2, are they dated and signed? Show me.

Dated November 2, initialed. Here. And his in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has no comma splices and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here they are side by side. The school's AI checker also says 94 percent, which I'd put last.
Okay. Put the September 24 sample and the essay side by side, and send me both pages. I'll read them tonight.

So here's my offer. Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I can run it Thursday, November 12, at 3:30 in the library, supervised by the vice-principal, Ms. Dunn, not me.

Thursday is tomorrow's next day, and Owen can't sit it cold, so I want Owen heard first. Put the terms in writing: private, not in front of his class, the zero withdrawn today, and nothing on his record in any form. Then I'll answer about Thursday.

Agreed. I'll withdraw the zero from the gradebook tonight. Owen can talk to me first, Wednesday at lunch, if he wants. The rewrite is private, in the library, not in front of his class. Nothing goes on his record. You'll have it in writing tonight, principal copied.

Okay. Put it in an email yourself, with the zero withdrawn and nothing on his record in any form. And one more thing: I'm not agreeing that Owen did anything. I'm agreeing to this so it stops touching him.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

To: Hale
Cc: Principal
Subject: Owen Kalinowski, English 30-1, follow-up to today's meeting

Hale,

As agreed today, you will withdraw the zero on Owen's Hamlet essay from the gradebook tonight, Tuesday, November 10.
Owen will have a private supervised rewrite in the library on Thursday, November 12, at 3:30, supervised by Ms. Dunn, not by you.
Owen may speak with you first on Wednesday, November 11, at lunch, if he chooses.
Nothing about this concern will be placed on Owen's record in any form.
Your written confirmation of these terms is due by 9 AM Wednesday, November 11.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: fallback position, with a private supervised rewrite agreed and the zero withdrawn.
Moved at: "Agreed. I'll withdraw the zero from the gradebook tonight."
Slipped at: "Okay. Put it in an email yourself, with the zero withdrawn and nothing on his record in any form."
